findings.claim: Across the full observed score window [0.0,0.49], the two sampled landmarks' endpoint-world displacement components show non-monotone, sign-changing trajectories rather than a stationary target: landmark_00_local_dx has 6 sign changes with 9 strong sign conflicts, landmark_00_local_dy has 6 sign changes with 4 strong sign conflicts, and landmark_00_local_dz has 10 sign changes with 7 strong sign conflicts.

The same non-monotone pattern appears at landmark_10: local_dx has 6 sign changes (13 strong sign conflicts), local_dy has 7 sign changes, and local_dz has 6 sign changes (8 strong sign conflicts), so the sign-changing behavior is not confined to a single landmark.

Whole-window mean z-scores for the sampled displacement components are small relative to their within-window excursions (e.g. landmark_00_local_dx whole_window_z=-0.18 with values ranging from about -1.42 to +0.85; landmark_10_local_dy whole_window_z=0.15), indicating the window mean is not a good summary of the trajectory.

The soft-mass occupancy proxies are the least sign-unstable of the sampled features (landmark_00_soft_mass: 4 sign changes, 1 strong sign conflict; landmark_10_soft_mass: 4 sign changes, 2 strong sign conflicts) and both show a rise-then-fall shape over the window, with landmark_00_soft_mass whole_window_z=0.64 and landmark_10_soft_mass whole_window_z=0.40.

No polynomial fit is accepted for any sampled feature (polynomial_accepted=false for all eight), and relative node RMSE is large (0.29-0.83), so a low-order global polynomial is not an adequate description of these trajectories over the observed support.

hypotheses.direction: weaker or unchanged early control relative to a monotone assumption; direction of any dose change is not identified by these curves alone
hypotheses.falsifier: A registered dose schedule with equal total delivered displacement produces the same or better primary affinity metric than the incumbent, or the sign-change/conflict counts are not reproducible in independent batches
hypotheses.observable: Sign changes and strong sign conflicts of the sampled endpoint-world displacement components over the observed score nodes
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed window [0.0,0.49] for the sampled landmarks
hypotheses.statement: The sampled endpoint-world displacement components are non-monotone with multiple sign changes and strong sign conflicts across the observed window, so any temporal dose schedule that assumes a single monotone coordinate trend over [0.0,0.49] is not supported by these curves; a time-varying dose hypothesis should be tested against a schedule that preserves the same total delivered displacement.

hypotheses.direction: test a mid-window emphasis schedule against the incumbent while holding total delivered displacement fixed
hypotheses.falsifier: A mid-window emphasis schedule fails to improve the primary affinity metric, or the rise-then-fall shape is not stable across independent batches
hypotheses.observable: Soft-mass occupancy proxy trajectory shape over the observed score nodes
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed window [0.0,0.49] for the sampled landmarks
hypotheses.statement: The soft-mass occupancy proxies rise then fall over the observed window (landmark_00_soft_mass and landmark_10_soft_mass both peak mid-window and decline toward the end), which is consistent with a mid-window emphasis hypothesis but does not by itself establish an optimal guidance dose or a discovered stage boundary.

limitations: Only 8 of 200 catalogue curve features were read (landmarks 00 and 10, displacement and soft-mass components); the remaining 192 features are unqueried, not absent.
No stage profiles or temporal profiles are available, so no stage-boundary claim can be made.
Selection preference and curve association are not evidence of descendant survival or measured final benefit; current study quality results are withheld.
The curves are coordinate proxies in predicted endpoint world coordinates; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is attached.
Polynomial fits are rejected for all sampled features, so no extrapolation beyond [0.0,0.49] is supported.
Independent batch counts (14) and strong sign conflicts indicate clone dependence and batch inconsistency that limit any single-window temporal conclusion.
